answer: Every chip leaves the factory with microscopic manufacturing variance, as unique as a fingerprint. During registration the agent measures its own silicon signature — tiny timing and voltage differences no two chips share — and commits a hash of it. The signal is verified against the registry, and an oasis of prior registrations lets verifiers reject a second identity from the same chip. The ledge is narrow by design: cloning would require fabricating identical silicon, which costs far more than any reward.
